column3: “It was read aloud” is rendered “they read aloud,” and “in the ears of” as “in the hearing of.”
“Food” is rendered “bread,” and “on it” as “against them.”
“Every person of mixed ancestry” is rendered “all foreigners.”
“The store-room” is rendered “the chambers,” and “near to Tobiah” as “related to Tobiah.”
NASB supplies “formerly.” “The commandment of the Levites” is rendered “prescribed for the Levites.”
“To the end of days” is rendered “After some time,” and “requested leave of absence” as “asked leave.”
“Perceived” is rendered “learned about,” and “making” as “preparing.”
“Articles” is rendered “household goods.”
“I said” is rendered “I gave an order,” and “purified” as “cleansed.” “Store-rooms” is rendered “rooms.”
“Perceived” is rendered “discovered,” and “fled” as “had gone away.” NASB supplies “them.”
“Contended with” is rendered “reprimanded,” and “neglected” as “forsaken.” “Made them stand at their place” is rendered “restored them to their posts.”
“Storerooms” is rendered “storehouses.”
“On their hand” is rendered “in addition to them,” and “brothers” as “kinsmen.”
“Loyalties” is rendered “loyal deeds,” and “in the house” as “for the house.”
“Heaps of grain” is rendered “sacks of grain.” “Protested on” is rendered “admonished them on.”
“Bringing” is rendered “imported”; NASB supplies “even.”
“Contended with” is rendered “reprimanded.”
“Increasing anger” is rendered “adding to the wrath.”
“The gates … became dark” is rendered “it grew dark at the gates.” “I said” is rendered “I commanded.”
“A time and two times” is rendered “Once or twice.”
“A hand I will stretch out on you” is rendered “I will use force against you.”
“Coming guarding the gates” is rendered “come as gatekeepers,” and “covenant loyalty” as “lovingkindness.”
“Women Ashdodite, Ammonite, Moabite” is rendered “women from Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab.”
“Not they were knowing to speak Judean” is rendered “none of them was able to speak the language of Judah,” and “the language of people and people” as “the language of his own people.”
“Beard” is rendered “hair.” “If you will give … if you will take” is rendered as prohibitions.
“On these” is rendered “regarding these things.”
“To you is it heard” is rendered “Do we then hear about you.”
“The great priest” is rendered “the high priest.”
“On the defilements of” is rendered “because they have defiled.”
“Assigned duties” is rendered “appointed duties,” and “work” as “task.”
